report.source_text: A 24-year-old woman presented to our dermatology clinic with a left posterior auricular papule and left preauricular papule present for 8 and 4 months, respectively (Figure 1). The patient had no significant medical or social history, including no tobacco or heavy alcohol use. Both lesions were painful and progressively enlarging. The patient denied any other symptoms.

report.source_text: Due to multifocal cutaneous disease, there was high clinical suspicion of metastatic disease. Our patient was referred to medical and surgical oncology for further evaluation, and computed tomography (CT) scans of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis were performed. Innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 1.8-cm hypoattenuated hepatic lesion, and prominent bilateral axillary lymph nodes were noted, all consistent with metastatic disease.

report.source_text: Shave biopsy was taken of both lesions.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old woman presented with progressive painful left posterior auricular (8 months) and preauricular (4 months) papules. Shave biopsies of both lesions revealed cellular dermal proliferations of epithelioid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in cords within myxohyaline stroma, with subtle intracellular vacuoles containing red blood cells (blister cells). Histological and immunohistochemical findings were consistent with EHE. Staging CT imaging demonstrated innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 1.8-cm hypoattenuated hepatic lesion, and prominent bilateral axillary lymph nodes consistent with metastatic disease. After oncology consultation, the patient elected watchful waiting with serial CT surveillance every 3 months.
